question:
A student makes the claim:</br></br>
“During sunset, the Sun appears red because **red light is scattered more** by air molecules.”</br></br>
Assume Rayleigh scattering is applicable in the clear atmosphere with $I_s\propto \dfrac{1}{\lambda^4}$. Evaluate the claim and give the correct physical reasoning.

options.A: Correct; red is scattered more because it has higher energy.
options.B: Correct; red is scattered more because it has longer wavelength.
options.C: Incorrect; shorter wavelengths (blue/violet) are scattered much more, so along the long atmospheric path at sunset, blue light is scattered out of the line of sight and the transmitted light becomes richer in red/orange.
options.D: Incorrect; the Sun looks red mainly due to total internal reflection in air.
